 ‘Just as white sunlight through stained glass separates into many colours, so the eternal Unity
breaks up into the many lives and objects of earthly existence. Colour, though beautiful, “stains” white
light; death shatters our separate lives, but reunites us with “the One”. All the beauty and art of ancient
Rome is inadequate to convey this total glory embodied in it’ (GM). The language, imagery, and thought
in this stanza are in a Platonic idiom, but cannot persuasively be referred with precision to any particular
